phase_0_hazard.ask: Where are you up to? Has anything formal happened yet?
phase_0_hazard.note_to_user: Whatever you say here, everything below still applies. This only tells us which words will make sense to you.

phase_0_hazard.ask: Are you under any court order, release or bail condition, undertaking, protection or restraining order, or a workplace directive?
Does it include no-contact, non-association, or stay-away conditions?
phase_0_hazard.note_to_user: We are not interpreting your conditions. Only your lawyer can. This just tells us which options to leave out.

items.text: Do not contact the other person. Any channel, any intermediary, no exceptions — including replying to them, and including through a friend or family member.
Do not look at their accounts, profiles, or posts. Viewing can notify them, and some platforms add you to a conversation just for opening it.
items.why: One of the most common ways people breach a condition without meaning to.

items.text: Do not delete OR CANCEL anything — not a message, photo, app, booking, subscription, or calendar entry. Not even one that embarrasses you. Not even one you never created and never wanted.
items.why: Deleting looks like consciousness of guilt and can be a separate offence. Cancelling is worse than useless: it often NOTIFIES the other side and can remove you from a channel in a way they see. Preserve, don't purge.

items.text: Read your e-mail normally. But do not CLICK a link in any message about this, and do not open or extract an attachment from one.
items.why: Reading is fine. A link is not: it often carries a code unique to you, so following it writes a dated entry, TODAY, into the very record your lawyer is about to ask for. Save the whole message as a file and let them open it. If you need to know where a link goes, tell your lawyer rather than finding out.

items.text: Do not create a second or anonymous account to look at anything.
Do not explain yourself to police, an investigator, HR, or the other person's friends. Not to clear it up, not informally, not at your own door.
items.why: Anything you say becomes a fixed account you are held to later — before you or your lawyer know what is actually alleged. You carry no burden to prove where you were.

items.text: Do not go anywhere you know the other person to be — including places you only recently learned they go, and including a TYPE of place or area they are known to use, not just a specific address.
items.why: Being accused teaches you things you must now avoid, and you cannot un-learn them. The condition can bite on knowledge you only acquired because of the accusation.

items.text: Do not try to tidy up or fix a shared group, album, folder, or subscription you are both in.
items.why: Leaving, un-sharing, removing yourself and cancelling all NOTIFY. Trying to fix a hazard is usually a fresh, dated, attributable hazard. Tell your lawyer instead; leave it exactly as it is.

items.text: Before signing up, booking, joining, or registering for anything at all, stop and check it against your conditions.
items.why: One tap can put your name on a list, add you to a chat, or place you somewhere. This is the single most common way an ordinary day becomes an allegation.

items.text: Do not consent to anyone searching or taking your phone or computer. Say you want your lawyer.
items.why: Consent replaces the safeguards that would otherwise apply, and it cannot be withdrawn once the data is taken.

items.text: Do not ask anyone what they remember, and do not ask anyone to write anything down for you.
items.why: It can be characterised as coaching or interference, and it contaminates the very recollection you were hoping to preserve. Give your lawyer the names; they take the statements.

items.text: If the other person contacts YOU, that is not your breach — but replying, even once, even to say stop, can be.
items.why: Do not respond. Do not block-and-delete either: preserve it exactly as received and tell your lawyer the same day.

items.text: Write down what you remember ONCE, as soon as possible, and then never improve it.
items.why: A note that gets tidied, expanded or corrected later is worth far less than a rough one written immediately — and the edits themselves become a problem.

items.text: If an allegation is dropped, withdrawn, or 'sorted out', change nothing. Keep every condition and keep every record.
items.why: Nothing is over until your lawyer tells you it is over, in writing.

phase_0_hazard.ask: Has anyone asked to look at your phone or computer, taken one, or shown you a warrant for one?
options: yes, they have one or took one
phase_0_hazard.note_to_user: We are not interpreting anything and this changes nothing about your conditions. It only decides where this tool puts files and what it refuses to write down.

phase_0_hazard.ask: Do you have a lawyer yet?

phase_0c_positive_obligations.ask: Does anything you have been given require you to DO something — report, notify a change, surrender an item, attend somewhere, keep in touch with someone?
phase_0c_positive_obligations.note_to_user: Not doing a required thing counts the same as doing a forbidden thing. We are not interpreting your paperwork — only your lawyer can.

phase_0c_positive_obligations.ask: Are any of them on a deadline or a schedule?

phase_0c_positive_obligations.text: Put every required act and its date somewhere you cannot miss it, and tell your lawyer about each one. A missed date is the easiest breach there is.

phase_0c_positive_obligations.title: Keep a proof ledger
phase_0c_positive_obligations.text: For every required act, keep proof you did it — a receipt, a confirmation, a sent message, a photograph, a note of who you spoke to and when. Also record every FAILED ATTEMPT: if you tried to comply and could not, that attempt is evidence and it disappears if you do not write it down the same day.
If you are unsure whether something is required of you, ask your lawyer before the date passes — not after.

phase_1_clock.ask: Roughly when did the event you are being accused about happen?
Is there a specific window in dispute — a date, and roughly which hours?
phase_1_clock.note: Widening every third-party request by a day either side is the default regardless. methods/03

phase_2_layers.ask: Were you wearing a smartwatch, fitness band, or smart ring during that time?
Did you have your phone with you?
phase_2_layers.priority_note: Shortest clock of any device-local layer. Do this first.

phase_2_layers.ask: Is it an Android or an iPhone?
Did you use a laptop or desktop around that time?
Were you messaging anyone about this, or with the other person?
phase_2_layers.warning: Export the whole thread. Selected screenshots are worth close to nothing. Do NOT open the thread if a no-contact condition applies — ask your lawyer first.

phase_2_layers.ask: Was any booking, registration, order, ride, or ticket involved?
Were you in a building with door fobs or cameras — home, hotel, office, gym, or a venue?
phase_2_layers.priority_note: Most perishable layer that exists. If nothing else gets done today, do this.

phase_2_layers.ask: Did you use a card, bank account, or transit pass during that window?
Did you travel in or out around then?
Did you take any photos or videos around that time?
Are there any injuries on your own body?
phase_2_layers.priority_note: Injuries heal in days. This is a today task, and it is the only layer that expires from your own body.

phase_2_layers.ask: Did anyone see you, or were you with anyone?
phase_2_layers.warning: Write the names down for your lawyer. Do NOT approach anyone yourself.

phase_2_layers.ask: Were you given any paperwork — a form, a notice, a printed sheet of conditions, a card?
